skill.name: limrun-gradle
skill.description: Build, sign, and publish Android applications through Limrun remote Gradle sandboxes for native Android, React Native, and Expo projects.
skill.summary: Run remote Android builds, produce signed artifacts, and support Play Store delivery.
skill.author: limrun-inc

security_audit.summary: Of 104 static findings, 102 are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, ordinary documentation, or defensive secret references. Two credential-handling findings are confirmed, and semantic review identified remote source transfer, signing-key escrow, password exposure, and direct Play Store publication.

remediation.issue: Project sources are synchronized to a third-party build service.
remediation.suggestion: Require confirmation before the first sync and show which files will upload, including files added through include rules.

remediation.issue: Signing keys can be generated or escrowed by Limrun.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit consent and document key access, encryption, export, rotation, deletion, retention, and recovery controls.

remediation.issue: The example passes signing passwords through process arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Remove password arguments from examples and require protected environment variables, secure input, or a credential manager.

remediation.issue: Play publishing accepts a reusable service-account JSON file.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer short-lived, least-privilege credentials and require confirmation before transmitting any service-account file.

remediation.issue: A build command can publish directly to Google Play.
remediation.suggestion: Add a mandatory confirmation showing package, track, artifact, signing identity, and version code before publication.

content.user_title: Build Android Apps with Remote Gradle
content.value_statement: Local Android builds require large toolchains and can vary across machines. This skill runs Gradle remotely, signs artifacts, and supports Play Store delivery.
actual_capabilities: Synchronizes an Android project to a Limrun sandbox and runs its Gradle wrapper.
Builds native Android, React Native, and Expo projects without a local Android toolchain.
Selects Gradle tasks, nested project roots, Expo app directories, and target ABIs.
Uploads APK or AAB artifacts and supports installation on a Limrun Android instance.
Signs release bundles with generated organization keys or user-provided upload keys.
Publishes signed bundles to Google Play using supplied credentials and version handling.
limitations: Requires the Limrun CLI, a Limrun account, authentication, and network access.
Project sources and selected credentials leave the local environment for remote processing.
iOS builds and detailed emulator interaction require separate Limrun skills.
Dynamic application identifiers and computed version codes may require explicit manual configuration.

use_cases.title: Build Without Android Studio
use_cases.description: Produce a debug APK from a development machine, container, or CI environment without installing the Android SDK.

use_cases.title: Test Cross-Platform Android Builds
use_cases.description: Build React Native or Expo Android projects remotely and deliver an APK for emulator testing.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Store Release
use_cases.description: Create a signed AAB, manage version codes, and publish an approved artifact to Google Play.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Debug APK
prompt_templates.prompt: Build the Android project in {project_path} remotely. Return the artifact location and summarize any build errors.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Specific Gradle Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Build {project_path} with Gradle task {task}. Use project root {gradle_root}, fix failures, and rebuild until successful.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Signed Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a signed release AAB for {application_id}. Use the approved signing key and upload the artifact as {asset_name}.

prompt_templates.title: Publish an Approved Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Publish {project_path} using {credential_method}. Select a free version code, report the package and artifact, then request confirmation before publishing.

output_examples.input: Build the current Android project as a debug APK.
output_examples.output: The remote build succeeded. The debug APK was uploaded as mobile-debug.apk and is ready for installation.

output_examples.input: Create a signed release bundle for the existing Play listing.
output_examples.output: The release bundle was signed with the approved upload key. The artifact is available as mobile-release.aab.

output_examples.input: Publish the approved Expo Android release.
output_examples.output: The package and next version code were resolved. Publication is awaiting confirmation with the selected artifact and signing identity.

best_practices: Review the upload scope before syncing proprietary projects or force-including ignored files.
Use protected environment variables or a credential manager for passwords and access tokens.
Confirm the package, version code, track, artifact, and signing identity before publishing.
anti_patterns: Do not commit keystores, service-account files, passwords, or access tokens to the project.
Do not publish a release before verifying the intended application identifier and version code.
Do not force-sync ignored files without checking them for secrets and unnecessary artifacts.

faq.question: Does this require Android Studio?
faq.answer: No. The Gradle wrapper and Android toolchain run in a remote Limrun sandbox.

faq.question: Which project types are supported?
faq.answer: The workflow supports native Android, React Native, and Expo projects that can produce Android artifacts.

faq.question: Can it build both APK and AAB files?
faq.answer: Yes. Choose the appropriate Gradle task or use signing options for a release AAB.

faq.question: Where does the source code go?
faq.answer: Selected project files are synchronized to Limrun infrastructure for the remote build.

faq.question: How are signing keys handled?
faq.answer: Limrun can generate an organization key or receive a user-provided key. Key escrow requires careful approval and governance.

faq.question: Can it publish directly to Google Play?
faq.answer: Yes. Publishing requires approved Play credentials, an existing listing, a unique version code, and explicit release confirmation.
